name: Creative Energy Core Steam System (downtown)
operator: Creative Energy Vancouver Platforms Inc. (formerly Central Heat Distribution Ltd.)
status_date: operating since 1968; CPCN C-5-22 2022-09-15; under construction per operator 2026
capacity_MW: unverified (~237 MW 2014 figure not found in a primary source); min. customer demand on gas boilers ~18 MW (BCUC C-5-22)
connected_today: ~200+ buildings (BCUC G-310-21A 2021; C-5-22 2022); 210+ bldgs and >14 km pipe (CoV RR 2023-07-11); operator claim >205 customers and >45 million sq ft
planned: Phase 1: 2 x 6.9 MW electric resistive steam boilers (13.8 MW; ~122,000 MWh/yr), 69 kV line from Murrin substation; space for 2 more 6.9 MW; later phases: convert steam piping to hot water (operator claim)
sources_of_heat: natural gas boilers at 720 Beatty St (FortisBC Rate 7); RNG bridging fuel rate approved by BCUC; electric boilers under construction
accepts_outside_heat: limited: chiller waste heat from Beatty St developer building to preheat boiler makeup water (~3,500 MWh/yr); heat pumps ruled out because they cannot reach steam temperature (C-5-22)
outside_heat_terms: no general third-party heat tariff found
location_source: 720 Beatty St plant; downtown core distribution (CoV established NE systems map 2020)
notes: Steam cannot take 25-45 C data-centre heat directly. 2023 CD-1(818) rezoning referral proposed adding 'bulk data storage' (data centre) use at 120-150 W Georgia/720-770 Beatty with 'synergies' with the energy centre; outcome of public hearing unverified. Operator gives completion 2026 and 2027 on same page.

name: Creative Energy Northeast False Creek (NEFC) hot water network
operator: Creative Energy Vancouver Platforms Inc. (part of Core TES)
status_date: franchise agreement 2014-05-26; first NEFC occupancy targeted Q2 2016 (CoV 2015); referenced as existing in BCUC G-310-21A (2021) and C-5-22 (2022)
planned: CoV NEFC page: west side on Central Heat steam; remainder to transition to new Creative Energy system
sources_of_heat: steam-to-hot-water conversion plants fed by Core Steam System (gas); low-carbon source considered but sewer heat not pursued (C-5-22)
location_source: NEFC and Chinatown (CoV report A2 2015-04-14; CoV NEFC sustainability page)
notes: Supplied from steam so effective temperature set by conversion plant; Franchise required low-carbon heat by 2020-01-01 (CoV 2015) - compliance unverified. 2018 CoV report: BCUC did not approve City-CE agreement; City considering owning NEFC systems (NEU expansion).

name: False Creek Neighbourhood Energy Utility (NEU)
supply_C: 65 (CoV heat pump diagram, undated); By-law 9552 s.5.3(g): building systems must need <=50 C supply when outdoor >0 C
return_C: 50 (CoV diagram); By-law s.5.3(c) min. 15 C delta-T
status_date: operating since 2010-01; sewage heat expansion online end 2024, completed 2025-10-16
capacity_MW: 32.7 total (2022, CoV RTS 14950); sewage heat 3.2 MW (2010) + 6.6 MW (2 x 3.3 MW, 2024) = ~9.8 MW (calc.)
planned: build-out ~2,000,000 m2 (2025 report); ~$85M thermal generation + $40M distribution; 100% renewable by 2030 being evaluated
sources_of_heat: sewage heat recovery (False Creek Energy Centre, 1890 Spyglass Pl; sewage in 25 C/out 20 C); natural gas boilers backup/peak incl. Mount Pleasant satellite peaking plant (2021); RNG; waste heat from customer buildings; 71% renewable (2025 fcst)
accepts_outside_heat: yes - customer-returned heat credited; 4 ETSs distribute customer solar/waste heat (CoV 2023, 2024); CoV reports name data centres as potential source; Expert Panel (2025-10-24) urges pursuing planned data centres
outside_heat_terms: By-law 9552 s.8.4(c): bill shows 'the number of megawatt hours of heat energy returned from the energy transfer station'; Sch. C Part 4: 'Credit for heat energy returned to energy transfer station $65.172 per each MW hour multiplied by 50%' (= $32.59/MWh, 2026). s.5.2(a)(v) permits 'equipment to recover waste heat energy from the refrigeration or cooling system of the building'. No clause for an independent third-party heat supplier found.
location_source: SEFC, False Creek Flats, NEFC, parts of Mount Pleasant (By-law 9552 Sch. A; CoV NEU page)
notes: Rates 2026: energy $65.172/MWh; capacity levy $10.466/kW/mo (Class 2/3). 2018 CoV report: MEC store in SEFC to sell waste heat to NEU. Brief's 67/50 C not found in a primary source. 2025 report says sewage expansion '6.6 MWh' (typo for MW). Data-centre heat would need a heat pump (65 C supply).

name: River District Energy (East Fraserlands)
return_C: within 60-85 range; separate return not stated
status_date: CPCN C-14-11 2011-12-19; Phase 2 CPCN C-3-23 2023-06-27; CEC completion expected 2025-03 (G-94-24); 2026-28 RRA filed 2025-09
capacity_MW: ~15 (temporary energy centres, 10 gas boilers); CEC 28 MW gas initially, expandable to 40; WTEF heat exchanger 10 MW
planned: build-out 2047: ~865,000 m2 residential + >46,000 m2 commercial; peak 26.1 MW (2047); 33 more ETSs
sources_of_heat: natural gas boilers; baseload from Metro Vancouver Burnaby Waste-to-Energy Facility (planned, delivered 90-120 C)
accepts_outside_heat: yes - contracted waste heat from WTEF
outside_heat_terms: TESPA with Metro Vancouver signed 2021-12-14, 30 yrs + 2 x 10 yr renewals, up to 10 MW baseload; levelized cost $54/MWh based on TESPA ceiling rate (prices in TESPA Sch. B, not public in decision)
location_source: East Fraserlands / River District (CoV established NE systems map 2020; BCUC C-3-23)
notes: CEC in-service not confirmed. Interim 2026 rates $0.81/m2/mo + $53.17/MWh. 2018 15 MW figure in brief matches TEC capacity.

name: UBC Academic District Energy System (ADES)
